# Cineview

> A landing-page framework in plain HTML. A page is a series of scenes, each with its own timeline, made of custom elements (cv-stage, cv-scene, cv-animate, cv-stack, cv-video, cv-fixed, cv-pause); the reader's scroll or finger moves through them. No runtime dependencies; it also works inside React or other framework pages.

Cineview's authoring goal is to help AI understand animation design and advise users. A plain-language brief or PRD should become a scene plan with content relationships, readable states, progress sources and checked implementation routes. This documentation goal does not imply a built-in AI service.

The package on npm is cineview@2.0.0 and later. The published 1.0.x versions were a different React API that this repository no longer contains; do not combine examples from them.

## Read by task

- [Design skill](skills/cineview-design/SKILL.md) ([Chinese guide](skills/cineview-design/README.zh-CN.md)): plan a landing page with the user first (what it is for, directions, how many scenes, each scene's content and material, a storyboard), then build it. References: working markup for video, images, type, line art and custom drawing; visual directions; 32 layouts; how the 41 references behave together in each mode; example page structures; ways to test a page.
- [AI design workflow](docs/ai/design-assistant.md) ([Chinese](docs/ai/design-assistant.zh-CN.md)): user recommendations, common page requests, PRD extraction, storyboards, element treatment and a worked image/text sequence.
- [41 design references and implementation routes](docs/ai/lexicon.md) ([Chinese](docs/ai/lexicon.zh-CN.md)): numbered original references with purpose, content relationships, framework primitives, page-owned work and missing capabilities. Look up relevant entries rather than asking users to choose from the whole catalog.
- [Landing-page design](docs/ai/landing-pages.md) ([Chinese](docs/ai/landing-pages.zh-CN.md)): reader goals, content relationships, progress sources, overlap and holding states, composition, media framing and acceptance.
- [Declaration and implementation conventions](docs/ai/declarative-design.md) ([Chinese](docs/ai/declarative-design.zh-CN.md)): grouped declarations, separator rules, configuration scope, progress and output ownership, extension points and verification. Named threshold configuration is a pending design, not an implemented API.
- [Documentation](site/src/content/docs/en/start/01-overview.md) ([Chinese](site/src/content/docs/zh/start/01-overview.md)): setup, input modes, timelines, progress sources, the first screen, states and events, every element and attribute, drag mode, custom drawing and migration from 1.x. Served at https://cineview.pages.dev/docs with live examples from site/public/examples/.

For a landing page, start with the design skill and agree on the scene plan. Open the documentation pages for exact attributes and behavior, and the other guides only when the task needs more depth. Check src/types.ts, src/jsx.ts, the parser and the input driver before relying on a detail. Parsing alone does not prove an effect is driven: verify it in a browser.

## Essential rules

- Load three things in <head>, in order: the head script (dist/head.js), cineview.css, then the module. Without the first two, animated elements flash on load.
- Each scene owns its timeline; there is no page-wide after sequence. `after` names an element of the same scene and waits for its entrance to end.
- `cv-stage input` is `scroll` (default) or `drag`. In ordinary scroll, entrances play on time once an element is in view (`enter`); in a zone (`cv-scene zone`) and in drag scenes, the reader's scroll or finger is the time (`scene`). `on` chooses another source; `enter` and `eye` are refused inside a zone.
- In a zone, 1 ms of timeline equals 1 px of scroll; the element that ends last sets the zone's length.
- `rise`, `grow` and `focus` already fade: adding `fade` to them puts two effects on one property.
- Content stays real text; every authoring error dispatches a `cv-error` event with a stable code. Listen for it while building a page.
